patient_has_finding_of_normal_cognition_.assessment: The patient is described as having six months of progressive cognitive and behavioral decline, significant memory impairment, inability to perform activities of daily living, poor delayed recall, disorientation, and inability to follow commands, all supporting abnormal cognition.

patient_has_undergone_neurological_exami.assessment: The neurological exam demonstrates clinically significant abnormalities, including paratonic rigidity, myoclonic jerks, and brisk reflexes, consistent with an abnormal exam.
patient_has_undergone_neurological_exami.evidence: Examination of the cranial nerves revealed clinically significant paratonic rigidity. Myoclonic jerks were seen in the arms, with symmetrically brisk reflexes.

patient_has_undergone_evaluation_of_psyc.assessment: The patient has significant cognitive and behavioral abnormalities described (progressive changes in cognition and personality, poor memory, unusual behaviors, functional loss, not oriented to year, inappropriate social behavior, and significant deficits on bedside mental status assessment) incompatible with a normal psychiatric state.
patient_has_undergone_evaluation_of_psyc.evidence: Six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality. He began to have poor memory, difficulty expressing himself, and exhibited unusual behaviors... unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently. He was alert and oriented to self and city but not year. He frequently interrupted the examiner. He could not spell the word 'world' backward, could not follow commands involving multiple steps and was unable to perform simple calculations. His speech was fluent, but he often used similar-sounding word substitutions.
